newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq, Lebanon to organise trade exhibition.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, Lebanon to organise trade exhibition.

text.p: Iraq and Lebanon signed an agreement on Thursday to organise a trade exhibition in Baghdad, their first since ties were cut in 1994, trade officials said.

"We sign an agreement today to hold a Lebanese food, medical and agricultural exhibition in Baghdad for the period between September 9 and 30," Faris Saad, head of the Lebanese Industries Marketing Company, told a news conference.
Lebanon cut ties with Iraq in 1994 after charging Iraqi diplomats with the assassination of an Iraqi opposition figure in Beirut.
But Lebanon now wants to sell Iraq food and medicine and buy oil from Iraq under Baghdad's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

The deal, which took effect last December, allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs for Iraqis, hard-hit by U.N. sanctions imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"I have reflected to the Iraqi officials Lebanon's desire to buy Iraqi oil under the deal," Saad said.
He said some 20 Lebanese firms including oil companies would visit Baghdad at the beginning of August to try to conclude oil and other trade deals.
The agreement on the exhibition was signed by Saad and the head of the Iraqi Agronomists Association, Mohammed Tahir, who said it would be the first step to resuming political and economic ties.
Saad said more than 150 Lebanese firms would take part and a bigger exhibition would be held next year.
Over the last three months both countries have been exchanging trade teams and their officials have hinted they were willing to resume political and economic ties.
"There are serious steps and an implied desire to resume relations," Saad added.

Iraq was disappointed by a Lebanese decision on Tuesday excluding Iraqi athletes from the Pan Arab Games, which start in Beirut on Saturday. Iraq ignored the decision and on Wednesday sent the athletes to the Syrian-Lebanese border to wait for visas.
"We were surprised at the decision. We hope it will not affect ties between Iraq and Lebanon...We also hope that the decision will be reviewed," Saad said.
